title: Nerv Rule Pack
description: Schema for spec/rulepacks/<name>.yaml — declarative guardrail rules loaded by the guardrails built-in at nervd startup. See docs/architecture/guardrails-builtin.md.

name.description: Pack name; matches filename minus .yaml. Globally unique across packs.

version.description: Pack format version. Bump on breaking change to rule entry shape.

description.description: One-line summary of what this pack guards against.

applies_to.description: Envelope filter. Pack only evaluated when the envelope matches.

tool.description: tool_use.name to match (e.g. 'Bash'). Single value in v1; array in future versions.

rules.description: Ordered list of rules. First match wins per pack; packs are evaluated in load order (alphabetical by filename).

id.description: Globally unique rule id (kebab-case, includes pack prefix). Used as config key in hooks.yaml.

severity.description: Risk level. Informational; does not change runtime behavior in v1.

pattern.description: Go regexp matched against tool_input.command. Use \b for word boundaries; remember Go regexp does NOT support lookaround.

default_mode.description: Mode applied when user has no override in hooks.yaml.

rewrites.description: Required if default_mode is 'rewrite' or if any user override may set 'rewrite'. Strategies applied in order.

destructive.description: If true, capture a backup before letting the command proceed (post-decision, pre-exec). Backup failure upgrades the rule to 'block'.

backup_strategy.description: Required if destructive=true. Names the capture method.

reason.description: Multi-line explanation surfaced in deny / ask UX. Should describe WHY the rule exists and what to do instead.

mode.description: Decision mode. allow=pass-through; block=deny; rewrite=mutate-then-allow; hitl=sync-prompt; manager=async-via-bus to manager profile; peer-N=N async approvals.

flag.description: The flag token to remove (e.g. '--no-verify'). Removes the flag and its value if any.

backup_strategy.description: Capture method. See ADR §Backup contract for semantics.
